builder_report.summary: Stage a ran as predeclared: FAIL, 1 of 3 families. JVP ratio B/C at rtol 1e-4 / 1e-6: grayscott2d 1.783 / 1.700 (pass), adr2d 1.454 / 1.496 (miss), bruss1d 1.122 / 1.276 (miss); step ratio 1.000 and equal achieved error in all six cells. Median family ratio 1.454, so the "<1.2 cancels v2" rule did not fire; v2 was not built because stage a did not pass, and the final discriminator is NOT_RUN. Client B0 (shipped cadence) matches protected arm A counter for counter in 6/6 cells. Residual audit: 0 failures in 8,704 declared solves (42,022 with exploratory); audit-on and audit-off runs are bit-identical; 0 allocations per step. Instructions C/B are 64-376x (merged kernel refactors per vector). The adr2d verdict depends on my predeclared choice to count the confirming residual JVP: Krylov vectors alone give 1.504 / 1.577 (2 of 3 families). Exploratory, not counted: a 300-vector basis leaves bruss1d at 1.20 / 1.29; linear rtol 1e-6 instead of 1e-10 cuts per-stage GMRES JVPs to 0.52-0.64x at unchanged error; the merged hook accepts residuals 5e4 times the protected threshold. Recommendation: do not keep the basis across steps.

open_issues: adr2d misses 1.5 by 0.3% to 3% (1.496, 1.454) and the outcome depends on a protocol choice I predeclared: the confirming true-residual JVP (one per solve, both arms) is counted. Counting Krylov vectors only gives 1.504 / 1.577, i.e. 2 of 3 families. The verdict stays FAIL as predeclared; the owner may want to rule on the counting.

Regime limit: the three stage-a families are mildly stiff by design (explicit DOP853 finishes them in 905, 1,673 and 10,625 RHS calls). Strongly stiff problems are covered by one exploratory cell only (standard Brusselator: arm A has 428 linear-solve failures in 865 attempts, B/C60 JVP ratio 0.947).
grayscott2d and adr2d have few attempts (14, 18 and 21, 45), including the ramp from initial step 1e-6.
Basis limit 200 was reached on bruss1d (73 and 6 fallback solves). Exploratory C300 gives 1.201 / 1.294, so the limit did not decide the verdict.

Exploratory finding worth an owner decision: the linear stopping test, not sharing, drives JVP counts. At linear rtol 1e-6, per-stage GMRES needs 0.52 to 0.64 of its 1e-10 JVPs at unchanged error; the merged hook with its own WRMS test uses 2.3 to 11.7 times fewer JVPs than B at similar error. Changing the protected tolerance is outside this node.

Exploratory finding: at loose linear tolerances the shared basis gives larger integration error than per-stage GMRES at the same residual bound (error ratio C/B up to 2.4 at 1e-6 and 40.6 at 1e-4). The correlated-residual explanation in the report is unverified.
Jacobi is the only preconditioner measured and does not help these families (B needs 1.01 to 1.36 times the JVPs); sharing under a strong preconditioner is unmeasured.
Wall time is diagnostic_only (shared host, load 3.9 to 6.2, no pinned core, single run).

Two exploratory groups started with 2 tracked files modified (parse_results.py and the contracts test); neither is in the measurement binary and the binary sha256 is the same as in the clean-tree groups.
robertson_rd1d (the fourth, final-only family) has a reference but no run.
Keeping the basis across steps was neither implemented nor measured; the recommendation against it is an inference from the per-stage breakdown.

Scope, protected files and commit order are clean; PREDECLARED (c563cb85, 00:37:03) precedes the first build of the measurement target (00:46:59) and the first declared run (00:57:42). Every frozen verdict reproduces: stage a FAIL, 1 of 3 (bruss1d 1.122/1.276, grayscott2d 1.783/1.700, adr2d 1.454/1.496, step ratio 1.000); cancel rule not triggered (median 1.454); final and kill NOT_RUN. I re-executed all six cells (36 arm runs): counters, states and audits are bit-identical, instructions within 2.5e-5. RESULTS.json and REPORT_KO.md regenerate byte-identically. My own JVP callback counter equals jvp_calls in 28 runs; my own residual arithmetic finds 0 failures in 7,312 solves. findings.claim: Arms B and C differ only in sharing the basis.
findings.evidence: B restarts every 40 columns (PerStageGmresOptions::baseline, krylov.rs:173-180; pass length at 478); C keeps one unrestarted basis of up to 200 vectors (219-225).
